title: SUPS
summary:
In computational neuroscience, SUPS (for Synaptic Updates Per Second), formerly CUPS (Connections Updates Per Second), is a measure of a neuronal network performance, useful in fields of neuroscience, cognitive science, artificial intelligence, and computer science.

SUPS is used to measure how quickly a computing system can simulate synaptic updates in neural network simulations. It serves as a benchmark for evaluating the computational power required to model biological neural networks and for comparing different hardware platforms used in neural simulation. The metric is particularly relevant for large-scale brain simulations where billions of synaptic connections must be updated in real time or near real time.

The transition from the term CUPS to SUPS reflects a shift in emphasis from abstract "connections" to the more biologically accurate "synaptic updates," aligning the terminology more closely with neuroscience conventions.
